chapters.title: Chapter 2: Who Needs to Pay Advance Tax

lessons.title: Salaried Employees: When TDS on Salary Is Not Enough

body.text: Your employer's TDS is designed to settle the tax on one thing: the salary that employer pays you. Every rupee you earn outside that payslip, and every job your employer does not know about, sits outside the net. That gap is where salaried advance tax comes from.

children.text: Most salaried people in India never think about advance tax, and most of the time they are right not to. Payroll does the work. But the moment a flat is let out, a weekend side project starts paying, or a job offer comes from a company with no office in India, the automatic system stops being complete. This lesson shows exactly where it breaks, and the two ways to fix it.
How Your Employer Works Out TDS

markDefs.definition: The annual certificate your employer issues showing salary paid and tax deducted. Formerly Form 16, it is Form 130 under the Income-tax Rules, 2026.

children.text: Under section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (old section 192), your employer estimates your salary for the whole tax year, applies the tax regime you have told payroll you will use, and spreads the resulting tax over your monthly payslips. At the end of the year it gives you a
showing what was deducted. The method is sound. Its limit is information: payroll only sees what payroll pays, plus anything you choose to tell it.

body.caption: Which salaried income your employer's TDS covers

cells: Paid through payroll and included in the annual estimate
Perquisites such as ESOP value on exercise
Taxed as salary and deducted by the employer; eligible startups may defer the deduction
Salary from a previous employer this year
Your new employer otherwise treats its salary as your only income
Salary from a foreign employer with no Indian entity
The employer has no Indian tax registration and deducts no Indian TDS
Payroll does not know about them unless you tell it
Capital gains on shares, including ESOP shares you later sell
Not salary, and no TDS applies to a resident individual's gains on listed shares

body.title: Quick Check: What Payroll Misses
body.question: Siddharth works at a listed IT company in Pune. Which of these is least likely to have been taxed through his employer's TDS?
options: His annual performance bonus paid in May
The perquisite value when he exercised his ESOPs in August
The capital gain when he sold those ESOP shares on NSE in February
The HRA portion of his monthly salary
body.explanation: The bonus, HRA and the ESOP perquisite at exercise are all salary, so payroll deducts TDS on them. Once he owns the shares, any gain on selling them is capital gains, not salary. No TDS is deducted on it, so unless it is small, it pushes him towards advance tax. Lesson 3 of this chapter covers investment income in detail.

children.text: The Most Common Gap: Income Outside the Payslip

Rahul is a 36-year-old engineering lead at a product company in Chennai, on the new tax regime. His employer deducts TDS correctly on his salary. On weekends he writes technical content for two small startups, and he lets out a flat he inherited in Velachery. Neither client nor tenant deducts any TDS.

body.title: Show me the math: Rahul's tax with and without his side income

content.caption: A shortcut: all of Rahul's side income falls in the 30% slab, in rupees

children.text: No rebate applies because his income is far above ₹12 lakh, and no surcharge applies because it is below ₹50 lakh.

body.label: Tax on Rahul's income that TDS does not reach
body.context: His employer deducts ₹3,19,800; his true tax is ₹4,50,216. The gap is far above ₹10,000, so he is liable for advance tax.

body.title: Rahul's ₹4,50,216 tax: who is paying it?

children.text: Side income that looks modest, ₹5,40,000 against a ₹25,00,000 salary, creates nearly 29% of Rahul's total tax. That is because it lands entirely in his top slab.

body.title: Try It: Pooja's Shop in Lucknow
body.prompt: Pooja earns a ₹15 lakh salary in Lucknow on the new regime, with TDS deducted correctly. She also lets out a small shop to an individual at ₹10,000 a month, with no TDS. After the 30% standard deduction on rent, and including 4% cess, how much extra tax does the rent create? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Annual rent is ₹1,20,000, and after the 30% standard deduction ₹84,000 is taxable. Her salary income after the ₹75,000 standard deduction is ₹14,25,000, and adding the rent keeps her within the ₹12 to 16 lakh slab taxed at 15%. So the extra tax is 15% of ₹84,000, which is ₹12,600, plus 4% cess, giving ₹13,104. That is over ₹10,000, so a ₹10,000-a-month shop is enough to make Pooja an advance taxpayer.

children.text: Two Ways to Close the Gap

Once you know the gap exists, you have a choice. You can pay it yourself as advance tax, or you can ask your employer to collect it through extra TDS on your salary. Under the old Act's section 192(2B), carried into section 392, an employee may give payroll details of income under other heads, such as rent or interest, and of TDS or TCS already suffered on them, in the prescribed form. The employer then factors these into your salary TDS.

body.title: Pay advance tax yourself, or route it through payroll?

columns.label: Pay advance tax yourself
points: Full control over estimates and timing
Works for any income, including irregular freelance fees and capital gains
You must remember four due dates and pay through e-Pay Tax
Miss a date and interest under section 425 applies

columns.label: Declare it to your employer for extra TDS
points: Tax is deducted automatically from each remaining payslip
TDS actually deducted counts in full against your liability
Best for steady, predictable income such as rent or FD interest
Late declarations leave fewer months to spread the tax, so take-home pay dips sharply

body.text: Declaring other income to payroll works best when you do it in April or May. Declared in January, the whole year's extra tax gets squeezed into three payslips. And payroll only deducts on what it pays you in future, so any instalment you have already missed stays your problem to fix with advance tax.

children.text: When There Is No TDS at All

Remote work has created a new kind of salaried taxpayer: someone employed full time by an overseas company, working from India, and paid without a single rupee of Indian TDS. For a resident, that salary is fully taxable in India, and every rupee of the tax is advance tax.

body.title: Scenario: Aisha's US Employer
body.scenario: Aisha, 31, is a resident of Bengaluru. She is a full-time employee of a US software company that has no office, subsidiary or tax registration in India. Her salary works out to about ₹40 lakh a year, credited monthly in dollars to her account and converted to rupees. The US company withholds no Indian tax. She has no other income and is on the new regime.
body.prompt: Does Aisha owe advance tax for tax year 2026-27? Estimate her tax, how much she should have paid by each due date, and a simple habit to stay on track.
body.modelAnswer: Yes. As a resident she is taxed in India on this salary, and with no Indian TDS the entire tax is uncovered. After the ₹75,000 standard deduction, taxable salary is ₹39,25,000. Tax is ₹3,00,000 on the first ₹24 lakh plus 30% of ₹15,25,000 (₹4,57,500), giving ₹7,57,500, and ₹7,87,800 with 4% cess. No surcharge applies below ₹50 lakh. Cumulative advance tax should be ₹1,18,170 by 15 June, ₹3,54,510 by 15 September, ₹5,90,850 by 15 December and ₹7,87,800 by 15 March. That is about 19.7% of her gross salary, so a practical habit is to move 20% of every salary credit into a separate savings account the day it arrives and pay each instalment from there. She should also keep her monthly salary slips and bank credit advices, because her AIS will show no TDS against this income, and she will need to show the tax was paid through her own challans.

body.text: Do not assume a foreign employer's US or UK withholding settles your Indian tax. If you are resident in India and working here, India generally has the right to tax that salary, and a double taxation claim is a separate and much slower process. Check your residential status and the tax treaty position with a chartered accountant before your first instalment.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Salaried Starting Point
body.textWithBlank: Under the new regime for tax year 2026-27, salaried employees get a standard deduction of ₹___ before slab rates are applied.
body.explanation: The standard deduction under the new regime is ₹75,000. It applies once per person for the year, even if you had two employers. That is one more reason two separate employer TDS calculations can together fall short.

body.title: Five Questions Every Salaried Taxpayer Should Ask in June
steps: Do I have any income that does not come through my current employer's payroll: rent, interest, dividends, freelance fees, capital gains or a foreign salary?
Did I change jobs this year, and if so, have I declared my previous salary and TDS to my new employer?
Is my employer applying the same tax regime I will choose when I file?
Estimate tax on the uncovered income at my top slab rate. Is it ₹10,000 or more after any TDS already deducted on it?
If yes, decide now: declare the income to payroll for extra TDS, or diarise the four advance tax dates and pay through e-Pay Tax

cards.definition: Requires employers to deduct TDS on salary based on the estimated salary they pay for the tax year.
Salary TDS certificate issued by your employer, formerly Form 16.
Giving your employer details of income under other heads and TDS or TCS already suffered, so salary TDS can cover the full picture.
₹75,000 off salary income under the new regime, allowed once a year.
The value of shares received on exercise, taxed as salary with TDS by the employer. A later gain on selling those shares is capital gains, with no TDS.
Deducts no Indian TDS, so a resident employee must pay the full tax on that salary as advance tax.

points: Employer TDS covers only the salary that employer pays, plus anything you declare to payroll
Rent, interest, dividends, freelance income and capital gains are common reasons salaried people owe advance tax
Side income usually falls in your top slab, so modest amounts create large gaps: ₹4.18 lakh of it cost Rahul ₹1.3 lakh
You can close the gap by paying advance tax yourself or by declaring the income to your employer for extra TDS, ideally early in the year
A resident working in India for a foreign employer with no Indian presence gets no TDS and must pay the entire tax as advance tax
Recheck in June and after any job change, rental agreement, new client or ESOP sale

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or investment advice. Section and form references are to the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026, with the corresponding 1961 Act references in brackets. Examples use new regime rates for tax year 2026-27 and ignore municipal taxes on property, as understood at the time of writing. Rules can change with each Union Budget. Verify current rules or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
